title: Ramayana Eyes Record ₹100 Crore Opening as Trailer Set for Comic-Con Debut
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's mythological epic starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash is poised to become the biggest non-sequel Bollywood opener, with its first trailer premiering at San Diego Comic-Con on July 24.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ramayana aims for a ₹100 crore opening, surpassing Adipurush's ₹86.75 crore record.
  • Trailer premieres at San Diego Comic-Con on July 24, targeting global audiences.
  • The film's budget is ₹900 crore, making it India's most expensive franchise.
  • Diwali 2026 release planned, with potential for an earlier October 30 date.
  • Distribution deal discussions are underway, valued at approximately ₹450 crore.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is set to become the first test of whether Indian cinema can sustain a production budget that rivals mid-tier Hollywood blockbusters. With Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Yash as Ravana, and Sai Pallavi as Sita, the mythological epic is targeting a ₹100 crore net opening day — a figure that would make it the biggest non-sequel opener in Bollywood history, according to trade analysts at Koimoi.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2065EYKOKQI

The current record for a non-sequel Bollywood opener belongs to Adipurush, which collected ₹86.75 crore net on its first day in 2023. Ramayana is expected to surpass that figure comfortably. The overall opening-day record remains with Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge at ₹145 crore net, and strong promotional material could push Ramayana toward ₹150 crore on day one, analysts say.

Comic-Con Premiere Signals Global Ambitions

The first trailer will premiere on July 24 at San Diego Comic-Con's Ballroom 20, a venue historically reserved for major Hollywood franchises. Producer Namit Malhotra and director Nitesh Tiwari will join lead actors Ranbir Kapoor and Yash for a panel featuring never-before-seen footage, live performances, and exclusive reveals, according to the official Comic-Con listing.

https://x.com/TradeBOC/status/2079959280732766213

The move positions Ramayana alongside properties like the Marvel Cinematic Universe, whose president Kevin Feige is scheduled for Hall H the following day. Following the international debut, the trailer will screen across thousands of theaters in India in multiple languages, including 3D and IMAX formats.

₹900 Crore Budget and a Zimmer-Rahman Score

Part 1 alone carries a reported budget of ₹900 crore, with a combined ₹1,600 crore budgeted for both installments — making Ramayana the most expensive Indian film franchise ever produced, according to Sacnilk, citing Bollywood Hungama sources close to the production. The visual effects are handled by DNEG, the eight-time Oscar-winning studio behind Dune and Interstellar. The score is a collaboration between Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.

"From Bharat to the world, the Ramayana trailer premieres worldwide on 24th July, 2026."

— The World Of Ramayana, official social media account

The cast extends beyond the three leads. Sunny Deol plays Hanuman, Ravi Dubey takes on Lakshman, while veteran actor Arun Govil — who played Ram in the iconic 1987 television series — appears as King Dashrath. Lara Dutta rounds out the ensemble as Kaikeyi.

The film is currently slated for Diwali 2026, with reports from Bollywood Hungama suggesting the makers are considering preponing the release to October 30 — a week before the festival — to build word-of-mouth ahead of the extended holiday window. Internal discussions on the date are reportedly underway, and a final decision hinges on locking distribution negotiations.

Those distribution talks have already generated headlines. Reports indicate the makers are in discussions for a theatrical distribution deal worth approximately ₹450 crore, reflecting the scale of expectations. Industry insiders predict the film could gross over ₹2,000 crore worldwide, which would surpass Baahubali 2's ₹1,788 crore record, according to Sacnilk.

Ground-Level Campaign Targets Next Generation

Beyond the global premiere, the team has launched a school outreach initiative in India titled "Hamara Satya, Hamara Itihaas." The campaign, which began on July 9, aims to reach over five lakh students across 400 schools in 18 cities through quizzes, drawing competitions, and interactive sessions focused on the epic's core values.

Release Strategy and Expectations
›Diwali 2026 release planned.

›Targeting to surpass Baahubali 2's ₹1,788 crore record.

For diaspora audiences, the Comic-Con premiere and a planned wide international release make this one of the rare Indian films designed for global theatrical dominance from the outset. Part 2 is scheduled for Diwali 2027.
